summary.text: The permafrost carbon cycle is the part of Earth's carbon cycle that moves carbon from frozen soils to plants and microbes, to the air, and back into the ground.
Because permafrost stays below 0 °C for years, it stores huge amounts of carbon: soils covering nearly 9% of land hold 25–50% of soil organic carbon.
As warming thaws permafrost and deepens the active layer, carbon stored for decades to millennia is exposed to processes that move it into the air.

facts.label: What counts as permafrost
facts.value: Below 0 °C for at least two consecutive years

facts.label: Compared with the air
facts.value: More than double the atmosphere's carbon

items.prompt: Permafrost holds vast amounts of organic carbon. Where does that carbon first come from?

options.label: Rock slowly breaking down in the cold
The frozen ground producing it itself
Plant matter worked down into the soil
Gas from the air freezing into the ice

items.explain: Permafrost does not produce carbon; organic carbon from land plants must enter the soil and then the permafrost to be stored.

items.prompt: Repeated freezing and thawing churns Arctic soil, for example by frost heaving. What does that do to carbon at the surface?

options.label: Carries it downward, at last into permafrost
Pushes it up and out into the air
Washes it out to sea in meltwater
Leaves it in place on the surface

items.explain: Cryoturbation mixes soil and moves carbon from the surface deeper until it can be incorporated into permafrost.

items.prompt: Why can carbon that ends up in permafrost stay out of the atmosphere for very long periods?

options.label: Microbes there turn it into solid rock
Permafrost changes only slowly with climate
The carbon is too heavy to rise again
Ice chemically destroys the stored carbon

items.explain: Permafrost stays frozen for long periods and responds slowly to climate changes, so stored carbon is kept from the air for a long time.

items.prompt: Permafrost-affected soils cover nearly 9% of Earth's land. Roughly what share of all soil organic carbon do they hold?

options.label: About 1–2%
About 9%
Over 90%
About 25–50%

items.explain: They store between 25 and 50% of soil organic carbon, far more than their share of land.

items.prompt: Average Arctic air temperatures climb year after year. What happens to the thawed active layer above the permafrost?

options.label: It thins, as the frozen ground pushes upward
It stays the same, as the ice below insulates it
It deepens, exposing old carbon to release
It refreezes, sealing the old carbon inside

items.explain: Warming extends thaw and deepens the active layer, exposing long-stored carbon to processes that send it into the atmosphere.

items.prompt: Peat keeps building up on top of frozen ground, so the surface slowly rises. What happens to the older soil now buried beneath?

options.label: It thaws out under the weight above
It becomes part of the permafrost
It is washed away by groundwater
It slowly burns off as methane

items.explain: As peat or sediment builds up and the permafrost surface rises, the deposited soil is incorporated into the permafrost.
